title: Clockwork Knight
subtitle: Midnight in the toy room
summary: Clockwork Knight is Sega's platform game, first released for Saturn in Japan on 9 December 1994.
body: Clockwork Knight is Sega's platform game, first released for Saturn in Japan on 9 December 1994. Pepper, a small toy knight, sets out to rescue Chelsea, whose voice brings the household's toys to life at midnight. The adventure takes him through rooms where ordinary furniture and possessions become enormous obstacles. Pre-rendered characters move through polygonal environments, with fully three-dimensional bosses adding another scale to the encounters. As one of Saturn's earliest games, it used this mixture to give a familiar side-scrolling journey the appearance of a miniature toy world.

Pepper's key provides his main attack. A quick thrust can stun an enemy, while repeated input twists the key into a more dangerous spinning motion. Stunned opponents and loose objects can also be lifted and thrown, including upwards. A nearby item may therefore become a weapon or a tool for reaching another part of the room. The player must judge jumps and deal with enemies before time or health runs out. Dying returns Pepper to the beginning of the level, making a successful route worth remembering.

The stages pass through children's bedrooms, a kitchen and an attic, with side areas offering treasures away from the direct route. Household objects supply the scenery and the obstacles, keeping Pepper's small size central to the adventure. Collected crowns can pay for continues or be risked in a bonus game after certain bosses. Hirofumi Murasaki's music accompanies the theatrical setting. The combination gives each room the character of a place already inhabited by toys, where a discarded object can become part of a knight's dangerous nighttime expedition.
